title: Scaling
tagline: Scaling laws, compute budgets, parallelism, low-precision training and hardware
summary: Language models improve predictably with scale. This course studies empirical scaling laws and compute-optimal training, estimates the FLOPs and memory of training runs, and explains how data, tensor, pipeline and expert parallelism, sharded optimisers and low-precision arithmetic spread training across thousands of accelerators.

chapters.title: Scaling laws
chapters.summary: Power laws relating loss to parameters, data and compute, and how they are measured.

chapters.title: Compute-optimal training
chapters.summary: Chinchilla-style allocation of compute between parameters and tokens, and over-training for cheaper inference.

chapters.title: Counting FLOPs and memory
chapters.summary: The arithmetic of a training step, activation memory, and estimating training time and cost.

chapters.title: Accelerators
chapters.summary: GPUs and TPUs, the memory hierarchy, arithmetic intensity and the roofline model.

chapters.title: Low-precision training
chapters.summary: Floating-point formats, bf16 and fp8 training, loss scaling and numerical stability.

chapters.title: Data parallelism and sharding
chapters.summary: Data parallelism, all-reduce, ZeRO and fully sharded data parallelism.

chapters.title: Tensor, pipeline and expert parallelism
chapters.summary: Splitting layers and models across devices, pipeline schedules and expert parallelism.

chapters.title: Running large training jobs
chapters.summary: Clusters and networking, fault tolerance, checkpointing and the engineering of very large runs.
